lead.hed: Benfold came home to Everett after eight months in the Pacific
lead.insight: The Navy said the guided-missile destroyer USS Benfold returned to Naval Station Everett on Oct. 16 after more than eight months of operations. The ship left San Diego on Feb. 1, steamed more than 20,000 nautical miles across the 3rd and 7th Fleet areas, and worked with forces from Canada, Japan, and the Republic of Korea, including exercises Valiant Shield 2026 and Freedom Edge. Cmdr. Rebecca M. Conti-Vock, the commanding officer, said the crew integrated fast and executed national tasking. The official photo of the return was taken and posted the same day.
lead.image_credit: Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Ryan Clark · DVIDS 10028612 · Public domain · USS Benfold (DDG 65) returns to Naval Station Everett after an eight-month deployment. Photo taken and posted Oct. 16, 2026.

political.hed: Providence says a fishing ban in the Central Arctic Ocean runs until 2037
political.insight: Friday's Providence essay covers last month's agreement among the United States, Denmark, and Greenland on Arctic security. It notes a 2017 deal by ten countries, including the United States and Russia, to ban commercial fishing in the Central Arctic Ocean from 2021 to 2037 while the waters are studied. The piece treats that ocean, more than a million square miles of international water, as the next place Washington and Moscow will compete over fishing, shipping, and mining.

political.hed: Law & Liberty reads Mangione through Crime and Punishment
political.insight: Friday's Law & Liberty essay says Luigi Mangione admitted killing UnitedHealthcare chief executive Brian Thompson in 2024, and that a federal charging document records the plea. The piece sets that killing beside Raskolnikov in Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment: a student who treats murder as a social good. It says Mangione is to be sentenced in December.

political.hed: American Reformer says America is reacting to a global order coming apart
political.insight: Friday's American Reformer essay says the plates of the global order started moving hard in the 2010s and have not settled. It argues that blaming Donald Trump and MAGA misses the point: in most respects they are reacting to events, not controlling them. American power is real, the piece says, and still not enough to hold a system that is coming apart.

tech.hed: Special Operations is fielding a lighter half-mask and goggles
tech.insight: Defense News reported Friday that U.S. Special Operations forces will adopt Avon Protection's MITR half-mask and goggles after the Pentagon and the company announced a contract on Oct. 9. The system is meant to guard against chemical hazards, lead powder from gunfire, and drug-lab chemicals including fentanyl. Avon told Defense News the goggles and mask can be worn together or apart, and that some units are already wearing the gear. A November 2025 Special Operations Command cancer study, cited in the same piece, found operators face an 18 percent higher cancer risk than other personnel.

tech.hed: The Army cased the colors of the 8th Psychological Operations Group
tech.insight: Defense News reported Friday that the Army inactivated the 8th Psychological Operations Group (Airborne) in a ceremony at Fort Bragg on Sept. 29. The Army's own release says Col. Robert Cusick and Command Sgt. Maj. Jason Montesanto cased the colors, and that inactivation keeps the unit's people and work inside the Psychological Operations Regiment rather than dissolving them. The group was formally activated on Nov. 16, 2013.

culture.hed: WORLD reports the Muellers still have no grave for Kayla
culture.insight: WORLD reports that Carl and Marsha Mueller wrote President Donald Trump on Nov. 6, 2025, before his meeting with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, asking for help bringing their daughter home. ISIS took Kayla Mueller hostage in Syria on Aug. 4, 2013, and reported on Feb. 6, 2015, that she had been killed. The couple told WORLD they have no grave and no marker. The Foley Foundation, cited in the same piece, reports at least 38 American citizens held by terror groups or hostile governments.

watch.hed: Theodore Roosevelt is the first visiting carrier to dock at Yokosuka in four years
watch.note: USNI's Friday Western Pacific Pulse says the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group docked Friday at Commander Fleet Activities Yokosuka, the first time in four years a carrier that is not forward-deployed there has done so. The same day's Keen Sword item names the cruiser Chosin and the destroyer Decatur alongside the carrier.
